title: Let the viewer run the commands it already shows, when it is served

needs: adr_003 refused execution on purpose and priced the reversal: a local server with authentication, a job model, and a decision about concurrent access to a file Blender may already hold. That price is now being paid deliberately, not discovered as a surprise later.

The menu bar already shows the exact command for List operations, Check setup and Preview pruning, and this session made that text copyable to the clipboard. A person still has to leave the page and paste it into a terminal to see the result.
`meshanvil view --serve` already runs an opt-in `http.server` on 127.0.0.1, port 0, for auto-refresh (adr_004). It currently serves `work/` read-only; nothing posts to it.
A page opened from `file://` has no server behind it at all and can never run anything -- the copy-to-clipboard behaviour just shipped has to stay its only option there.

`Refresh viewer` would restart the very server handling the request that triggers it, and `Create a runbook <report-id>` shows a placeholder id, not a real one -- neither is safe to wire to real execution in this slice.
context: The runner already refuses a busy target (target_busy) and already serialises identity allocation per project; this request does not re-implement that, it only serialises its own subprocess calls so two clicks on the same button cannot race each other.
The three commands in scope take no destructive action and no operator-supplied argument: they are the same closed set already printed in the menu, never a string typed on the page.

The port is already random per launch (port 0); a per-launch token embedded in the page's own data.js is the authentication adr_003 named, sized to a single-operator localhost tool rather than a login system.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Opened via `meshanvil view --serve`, each of List operations, Check setup and Preview pruning runs from its menu row and shows its stdout, stderr and exit code in the page; opened from a plain file, the same rows still only copy the command, exactly as they do today.

AC2: The server refuses to run anything unless the request carries the exact per-launch token embedded in that session's data.js; a missing or mismatched token is refused before any subprocess starts.
AC3: The server accepts only one of the three fixed named commands; any other value is refused, and nothing the page sends can become part of the command line.
AC4: A second run request arriving while one is still executing is refused, not queued, and the first request's result is still returned to whoever asked for it.
AC5: `Refresh viewer` and `Create a runbook <report-id>` stay copy-only in this slice; the cut is recorded as a backlog item rather than silently dropped.

AC6: adr_003 is marked Superseded by a new ADR that records the security boundary chosen -- localhost-only, per-launch token, one command at a time, a closed command set -- and states why it satisfies the price adr_003 named rather than reopening the question from zero.

product.title: A served viewer that can run what it already shows
product.overview: Reverses adr_003's refusal to execute, on the terms adr_003 itself priced: a local server, a per-launch token, and one command at a time, limited to the closed set of commands the menu already prints.
goals: Let the three safe, argument-free menu commands run from a served viewer page and show their result in place.
Keep a plain file:// page exactly as safe as it is today -- copy-to-clipboard, nothing more.
Record the reversal as a superseding ADR rather than editing adr_003's decision in place.
non_goals: Running `meshanvil run <operation> <source>` or any command that takes an operator-supplied argument.
A job queue, a task history, or cancellation of an in-flight command.
Authentication beyond a single per-launch token; no accounts, no login, no remote access.
Wiring `Refresh viewer` or `Create a runbook <report-id>` to real execution.

backlog_items.title: Run a closed set of commands from the served viewer's own server
problem: The `--serve` server only serves files; there is no way for the page to ask it to do anything.
adr_003 named the price of changing that -- authentication, a job model, a concurrency decision -- without paying it, so paying it now needs its own recorded decision, not a quiet code change.
Nothing today stops a page from sending an arbitrary string if a run endpoint is added without a closed command set and a token.
scope_in: One POST endpoint on the existing `--serve` server that runs one of List operations, Check setup or Preview pruning as a subprocess of `bin/meshanvil`, the same entry point a person would type.
A random token generated per server launch, embedded in `data.js`, required on every request to the endpoint.
Serialising the endpoint's own subprocess calls so a second request while one runs is refused outright.
Superseding adr_003 with a new ADR naming this exact boundary.
scope_out: Any command that takes a path, an operation name, or any other operator-supplied value.
A queue, retry, or history of past runs.
Changing what `--serve` does when no run is requested; file serving is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The endpoint runs exactly one of the three fixed commands by name, never a string from the request body.
AC2: A request without the current per-launch token, or with a stale one from a previous launch, is refused before any subprocess starts.
AC3: A request that arrives while another is executing is refused immediately; the request already running still returns its result.
AC4: adr_003 carries a Superseded status pointing at the new ADR, and the new ADR references adr_003's named price and states how each part of it was paid.

backlog_items.title: Show a command's own output where its text used to sit
problem: The menu's command rows currently only copy their text to the clipboard, on every kind of page.
A page opened from `file://` has no server to ask and must keep doing exactly that.
A page opened via `--serve` does have a server now, but nothing on the page knows to use it instead.
scope_in: Detecting whether the page was opened from `--serve` (location.protocol) or from a plain file, once, at load.
On a served page, the three in-scope command rows call the run endpoint instead of copying, and show stdout, stderr and exit code where the command text was.
On a file:// page, and for `Refresh viewer` / `Create a runbook <report-id>` on any page, the existing copy-to-clipboard behaviour is unchanged.
scope_out: Any visual redesign of the menu beyond showing a result in place of, or beside, the command.
Streaming partial output; the full result arrives once the subprocess finishes.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A served page running List operations, Check setup or Preview pruning shows the real stdout/stderr/exit code, not the copy-to-clipboard flash.
AC2: The same rows on a file:// page still only copy to the clipboard, byte-for-byte the behaviour shipped this session.
AC3: `Refresh viewer` and `Create a runbook <report-id>` copy on every kind of page, served or not.

orchestration_task.title: Let the viewer run the commands it already shows, when it is served
plan: Write the superseding ADR first: the exact boundary (localhost-only, per-launch token, one command at a time, closed command set) decided before any code depends on it.
Add the run endpoint to the existing --serve server: token check, closed command dispatch, single-flight guard, subprocess of bin/meshanvil.
Thread the per-launch token into data.js next to the other build-time payload fields.
Wire the three in-scope menu rows to the endpoint on a served page, rendering stdout/stderr/exit code; confirm file:// pages and the two out-of-scope rows are unchanged.
Extend viewer_smoke (served mode) and add a host-side check for the endpoint's token and single-flight refusal.
Mark adr_003 Superseded, cross-link it to the new ADR, and update adr_004's consequence note about the reversal cost.
Run make check, the fixture check and both smokes (file:// and --serve) before closeout.
